findings.title: doDiff stores stack address of flastcontent in rule->last_events (use-after-return)
findings.description: When check_diff detects a change, doDiff assigns the stack-local buffer flastcontent to rule->last_events[1] and returns. OS_CheckIfRuleMatch then returns to the main analysis loop, which calls OS_Log/OS_LogOutput and fprintf's last_events with %.1256s. That pointer is no longer valid. Default rule 533 enables check_diff for ossec: output: 'netstat -tan lines.
findings.impact: Any registered agent can trigger undefined behavior in ossec-analysisd: stack contents are leaked into alerts.log (and any mail/integrations that consume the alert), and under ASAN/hardening the process aborts. That degrades or takes down alert matching, AR, mailing, and integrations.
findings.attack_path: 1) Manager runs analysisd with stock ossec_rules.xml (rule 533). 2) Registered agent sends LOCALFILE/SYSLOG-shaped event: ossec: output: 'netstat -tan': ports-A (no syslog date so program_name stays unset; ossec decoder ^ossec: matches). 3) First event creates the diff file; no alert. 4) Agent sends a second differing line. 5) doDiff loads prior content into stack flastcontent, sets last_events[1]=flastcontent, returns. 6) OS_Log dereferences the dangling pointer while writing the level-7 alert.
evidence: Local ASan replica of stack pointer publish + post-return printf: stack-use-after-return
findings.remediation: strdup/heap-allocate the previous content before storing in last_events, or copy into a heap buffer owned by RuleInfo and free on the next diff. Never store addresses of automatic storage in rule->last_events.

findings.title: Rootcheck JSON parser injects attacker-controlled keys into the rule JSON object
findings.description: For rootcheck-grouped alerts, W_JSON_ParseRootcheck regex-captures {Name: values} from agent-controlled full_log and calls cJSON_AddItemToObject(rule, token, array) with the capture name as the key. Names may be level, comment, sidid, groups, etc. cJSON allows duplicate keys; PrintUnformatted emits both the real numeric level/comment and the attacker array. Short captures avoid the already-reported 30-byte sprintf overflow and trim(NULL) empty-name crash.
findings.impact: When jsonout_output is enabled (Wazuh install default), a registered agent can pollute alerts.json rule fields. Downstream SIEM/SOAR parsers that take the last duplicate key or assume level is a number can mis-prioritize alerts or fault on type confusion — alert-stream integrity break, not manager RCE by itself.
findings.attack_path: 1) jsonout_output yes. 2) Registered agent sends ROOTCHECK_MQ event that fires a rootcheck-group rule (e.g. 510). 3) Log contains a short token such as {level: 999} and/or {comment: pwned}. 4) Eventinfo_to_jsonstr -> W_ParseJSON -> W_JSON_ParseRootcheck adds those keys onto the rule object. 5) alerts.json contains duplicate level/comment keys.
findings.remediation: Allowlist compliance key names (e.g. PCI_DSS, CIS) or nest captures under a fixed compliance object. Reject keys that collide with reserved rule fields (level, comment, sidid, groups, frequency, firedtimes, info, cve).
